title: Modulo Arithmetic Game Strategy Analysis
approach_explanation: The game centers around whether the initial integer $n$ is divisible by 3. Since players can either add 1 or subtract 1, they can change the remainder modulo 3 by $\pm 1$. If $n \pmod 3 \neq 0$, Vanya (the first player) can immediately make a move to reach a multiple of 3 ($n \pmod 3 == 0$), winning on his very first turn. If $n \pmod 3 == 0$, any move Vanya makes will result in $n \pmod 3 \neq 0$ (either 1 or 2). Vova can then always reverse Vanya's move to bring the number back to a multiple of 3 on his turn, eventually winning since Vanya has a limit of 10 moves and cannot win from this position. Thus, Vanya wins if and only if $n$ is not a multiple of 3.

code_breakdown.explanation: Reads the number of test cases $t$ and loops through each test case to process the input integer $n$.
Checks if $n$ is divisible by 3 using the modulo operator ($n \% 3 == 0$). If true, outputs "Second" (Vova wins); otherwise, outputs "First" (Vanya wins).

complexity_analysis.time_justification: The solution processes each of the $t$ test cases in $O(1)$ constant time with a single modulo operation and a conditional check.
complexity_analysis.space_justification: Only a few primitive integer variables ($t$ and $n$) are used, requiring constant auxiliary memory.

strengths: Extremely concise and optimal time/space complexity.
Leverages game theory insight to reduce a multi-turn game to a single modulo check.
edge_cases_handled: Correctly handles initial values that are already multiples of 3.
best_practices_feedback: Using `\n` instead of `endl` is recommended in competitive programming to avoid unnecessary stream flushes.
Including `<bits/stdc++.h>` is fine for competitive programming, though standard modular headers are preferred for production.

optimization_and_alternatives.tradeoffs: The current modulo approach is already optimal in both time and space. No further algorithmic optimization is possible.
